new: _une théorie comme une autre_ — a theory like any other.
reason: Untranslated French phrase; a listener without French loses the point of the aside.

old: so much so that it would be almost ill-bred in a man of society
new: so much so that it would be almost ill-bred for a man of society to do it
reason: 'it would be almost ill-bred' has no clear subject on first hearing; naming the action restores the logic.
'It has acted violently' is opaque out of context; the sense is that the news has struck her violently.

old: I have nothing else to fear either. Because you couldn't complain afterwards.
new: I have nothing else to fear either, because you couldn't complain afterwards.
reason: Detached 'Because' fragment reads as a slip; joining it keeps the reasoning in one breath.

old: cocked it, and laid it in her hand on the table
new: cocked it, and rested her hand holding it on the table
reason: 'laid it in her hand on the table' is a garbled image; she rests her hand with the revolver on the table.

old: only gradually working her way to Third Street
new: only gradually working her way round to the everyday matters of Third Street
reason: 'working her way to Third Street' sounds like literal travel; the point is she circles back to homely local matters.

new: coming from a café chantant, a music-hall café,
reason: Period French term a listener may not know; a brief gloss unlocks the joke.

old: he had recommended Raskolnikov to entrust her
new: he had urged Raskolnikov to entrust her
reason: 'recommended someone to do' is ungrammatical in modern English.

old: with a copper Achilles helmet on his head
new: with a copper helmet like Achilles' on his head
reason: The watchman is then called 'Achilles' throughout; making the helmet comparison explicit tells the listener where the nickname comes from.

old: Dmitri Prokofitch brought it to me.
new: Dmitri Prokofitch — Razumihin — brought it to me.
reason: Listeners know him as Razumihin; the mother's formal name-and-patronymic form may not register as the same person.

old: Killing her was atonement for forty sins.
new: Killing her would earn pardon for forty sins.
reason: Proverbial Russian phrase is puzzling as literal 'atonement'; the sense is that killing her would wipe out forty sins.
